findings.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:46-48 — authorization uses `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)` to compute `isTeamAdminOrOwner`, which is logical AND of two mutually-exclusive-in-practice role checks, so a pure team admin (not also flagged owner) or a pure owner (not also flagged admin) both fail the gate, meaning the "OR" semantics implied by the variable name never actually admits the admin-only or owner-only case the code intends to allow (confidence 85, severity P1).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no `.max()`/length bound, so a single addGuests call can request unbounded attendee-row creation via `createMany` (line 92-100 of the handler) and unbounded email fan-out in `sendAddGuestsEmails`, with no pagination or batching boundary anywhere in the call chain (confidence 80, severity P1).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74-78 — de-duplication of guests against existing attendees is enforced only in application code (`guests.filter(...).some(...)`) between a read (`prisma.booking.findFirst` at the top of the handler) and a write (`prisma.booking.update` with `createMany` at line 92), with no unique constraint visible on the attendee table and no transaction/row lock, so two concurrent addGuests calls with the same guest email race past the check-then-insert window and both succeed, producing duplicate attendee rows for the same email (confidence 65, severity P2).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:70-77 — `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased (`.map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`) but the incoming `guest` value from `guests.filter(...)` is never lowercased before `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`, and likewise `guest === attendee.email` at line 76 is a raw case-sensitive comparison, so a blacklisted address submitted with different casing (e.g. "Foo@Bar.com" vs blacklisted "foo@bar.com") bypasses the block, and the same guest with varied casing bypasses the existing-attendee dedup, creating a second attendee row that is semantically the same person (confidence 80, severity P1).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92-168 — `prisma.booking.update` (persisting new attendee rows) is followed by `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with no surrounding transaction or compensating rollback path, so a failure in the calendar-provider update leaves newly-added guest attendee rows permanently committed in the DB while the external calendar event and any downstream state remain out of sync with no mechanism to detect or reconcile the mismatch (confidence 70, severity P2).

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:525-548 — sendAddGuestsEmails ignores all notification-gating flags honored by sibling sendScheduledEmails (hostEmailDisabled/attendeeEmailDisabled params, eventTypeDisableHostEmail/eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail from metadata.disableStandardEmails, and hideCalendarNotes stripping of additionalNotes), so organizers/attendees who opted out of standard emails via event-type settings still receive add-guest emails (confidence 85, severity P1).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:171-172 — sendAddGuestsEmails is called with only (evt, guests), no eventTypeMetadata/hostEmailDisabled/attendeeEmailDisabled arguments even though booking.eventType (and thus eventType.metadata) is already fetched in the same handler, so the disable-standard-emails feature silently regresses for this new code path (confidence 80, severity P1).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:1-8 and apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:24-56 — no maximum guest-count limit is enforced client-side or server-side (z.array(z.string().email()) has no .max()), so a single call can create an unbounded number of attendees/emails, with no rate limiting on the mutation either (confidence 75, severity P1).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:29-42 — the handler never checks booking.status (e.g. CANCELLED/REJECTED) or whether booking.endTime has already passed before adding guests and updating the calendar event, and BookingListItem.tsx wires the "additional_guests" action into bookedActions which is rendered for isBookingInPast bookings too, so guests can be silently added to cancelled or already-completed bookings (confidence 65, severity P2).

apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:59 — Dialog uses onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog} directly with no reset handler, so closing via backdrop click/Escape (as opposed to the Cancel button) leaves isInvalidEmail=true and stale multiEmailValue in state; reopening the dialog immediately re-shows the "emails_must_be_unique_valid" error banner for a fresh attempt (confidence 70, severity P2).

apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:47-56 — handleAdd only sets isInvalidEmail to true on failure and never clears it back to false on a subsequent valid attempt before the mutation resolves, and there is no per-field inline validation, so the generic error banner can persist behind a spinner instead of disappearing immediately when the user starts correcting input (confidence 55, severity P3).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts (whole file) and apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx (whole file) — no test files were added or modified for either the new tRPC mutation (permission checks for organizer/attendee/team-admin-owner, blacklist filtering, duplicate-guest filtering, EventManager calendar update, email send failure swallowing) or the new dialog component, despite this handler containing security-sensitive authorization branching (isTeamAdminOrOwner/isOrganizer/isAttendee) (confidence 90, severity P1).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:52-55 — isTeamAdminOrOwner requires isTeamAdmin(user.id, teamId) AND isTeamOwner(user.id, teamId) to both be true (logical AND, not OR as the variable name implies), so a plain team admin who is not also the owner is denied permission to add guests, which is likely an unhandled/untested requirement gap for team-booking guest management (confidence 60, severity P2).

apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:33 — no duplicate-submission guard beyond the mutation's own isPending flag driving the Button's loading prop; there is no explicit disabling of the Add button or debouncing, so rapid double-clicks before the loading state visually updates can fire two mutations for the same guest list (confidence 50, severity P3).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` has no try/catch; the guest attendee rows were already committed by the `prisma.booking.update` at line 92-106, so if this call throws (e.g. transient calendar-provider API failure), the DB and calendar go out of sync silently — the request fails with an unhandled 500 while guests remain persisted, and a client retry will re-run the whole handler against already-added guests. (confidence: high, P1)

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:167-171 — `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` swallows every email-send failure without logging the `err` object (message/stack lost) and without surfacing anything to the caller; the handler still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` at line 173, so the API reports full success even when no invite/notification email was ever delivered. (confidence: high, P2)

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:58-68 — `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow` is not wrapped in try/catch or converted to a TRPCError; if the organizer record is missing/deleted (e.g. race with user deletion) this throws Prisma's `NotFoundError`, which propagates as a raw, unhandled exception producing a generic 500 instead of a clean 4xx TRPCError like the NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN checks used elsewhere in the same handler (lines 44, 55). (confidence: high, P2)

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:525-550 — `sendAddGuestsEmails` (new in this diff) fans out all organizer/team/attendee emails via `Promise.all` with no per-call timeout visible in the added code; a single slow/hanging outbound email provider call will hold the whole request open (compounding with the already-swallowed error at addGuests.handler.ts:167-171) with no bound on latency. (confidence: medium, P3)

apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:98 — `<Button data-testid="add_members" loading={addGuestsMutation.isPending} onClick={handleAdd}>` only sets `loading`; `onClick={handleAdd}` is not additionally gated by `!addGuestsMutation.isPending` and `handleAdd` (lines 48-58) has no internal in-flight guard, so if the `loading` prop doesn't disable click handling on this repo's Button implementation, rapid double-clicks before the mutation settles can fire `addGuestsMutation.mutate` twice, submitting duplicate add-guest requests. Note: packages/ui Button source was not present in this checkout to confirm whether `loading` disables the underlying element, so this is flagged as a plausible risk rather than a confirmed defect. (confidence: low, P3)

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:70-77 — introduces a BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS env-var-driven email-blocking feature that is not implied by "add guest management functionality," a new unrequested configuration surface/behavior bundled into this change (confidence 65, P2).

apps/web/components/booking/BookingListItem.tsx:193-198 (only "add_members"/AddGuestsDialog action added) — the task is titled "guest management" but the entire delivered surface (menu item, dialog, schema, handler) only supports adding guests; there is no remove-guest or edit-guest capability anywhere in the diff, so "management" is delivered as "addition only," a meaningful under-scoping relative to the task title (confidence 70, P2).

apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-29 vs packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74-81 — client-side zod refine only checks uniqueness within the newly-submitted email array (via Set) and never checks against the booking's existing attendees, while the server silently filters out guests matching existing attendees/blacklist and only throws when zero guests remain; a guest already on the booking passes client validation but is silently dropped server-side with no per-guest error, so validation semantics diverge between client and server (confidence 60, P2).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74-77 — P0, confidence high: the guest blacklist check `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` compares the raw, non-lowercased incoming `guest` string against a lowercased `blacklistedGuestEmails` array, so any attacker submitting a blacklisted address with different casing (e.g. `Blocked@Example.com` vs `blocked@example.com`) bypasses the blacklist entirely, defeating the control's purpose (spam/abuse-domain blocking).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:26-56 — P2, confidence medium: `prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId } })` fetches the booking unscoped to the requesting user before any authorization check, so any authenticated user (any bookingId, including other tenants' bookings) can trigger the query and reach the permission-check branch; combined with the isTeamAdminOrOwner bug below, current effective authorization collapses to organizer-or-attendee, but the unscoped lookup pattern is fragile — a future edit to the `&&` (see next finding) or any bypass of isOrganizer/isAttendee reintroduces full IDOR to add guests/send calendar invites on arbitrary bookings.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:46-48 — P1, confidence high: `isTeamAdminOrOwner = (await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))` requires the caller to be BOTH team admin AND team owner simultaneously; in a normal team-role model these are typically mutually exclusive or owner is a distinct role from admin, so this condition can never evaluate true and the intended "team admin or owner can manage guests" authorization path silently never grants access. This is a logic bug that happens to fail closed today (not itself an authz bypass), but it is exactly the kind of bug a future contributor "fixes" by flipping to `||` without re-deriving the intended semantics — at that point it becomes a genuine privilege-widening change that must be verified against actual role semantics (is team owner a subset of admin, or a separate flag?) rather than reflexively swapped.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:52 — P1, confidence medium: `isAttendee = booking.attendees.find(attendee => attendee.email === user.email)` authorizes based on matching the authenticated user's own account email against a booking attendee record; if any account-creation or OAuth linking path in this codebase allows a user to set/claim an unverified email address on their own user record, an attacker can self-register with a victim's known email (e.g. a booking attendee's address) and pass this check to add arbitrary guests and trigger calendar-invite emails on someone else's booking. This handler does not itself verify `user.email` is confirmed; it trusts ctx.user.email as an authorization credential.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:1-8 — P1, confidence high: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no `.max()`/length cap on the array, so any authorized caller (including a mere attendee on a booking, per isAttendee at line 52) can submit an arbitrarily large list of external email addresses in a single call; each one triggers a real "AttendeeScheduledEmail"/"AttendeeAddGuestsEmail" send via `sendAddGuestsEmails` (packages/emails/email-manager.ts:525-550) from Cal.com's trusted sending domain, turning this endpoint into an unthrottled mass-mail/phishing relay against arbitrary third-party addresses under the guise of a legitimate calendar invite.

apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:42-45 — P3, confidence low: `onError` builds `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}` and shows it as a toast; `err.message` here is the fixed string literal thrown server-side (e.g. "booking_not_found", "you_do_not_have_permission") rather than attacker-reflected input or a raw exception, so this is low-severity internal-detail exposure (confirms booking existence/permission state to the caller) rather than a stack-trace/secret leak; suppressed as below the P0 bar but noted for completeness.

In the handler, the (potentially large) `guests` list is used to build `guestsFullDetails` and is persisted via `attendees.createMany` (addGuests.handler.ts around the `createMany` call), and then email sending fans out over `calendarEvent.attendees` (and team members) using `Promise.all` in `sendAddGuestsEmails` (packages/emails/email-manager.ts). With no `.max()`/batching/limits shown anywhere in the diff, a single call can trigger unbounded row creation and unbounded concurrent outbound email work, which is a verifiable DoS/perf/security defect exposed by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74-78 — de-duplication of guests against existing attendees is enforced only in application code (`guests.filter(...).some(...)`) between a read (`prisma.booking.findFirst` at the top of the handler) and a write (`prisma.booking.update` with `createMany` at line 92), with no unique constraint visible on the attendee table and no transaction/row lock, so two concurrent addGuests calls with the same guest email race past the check-then-insert window and both succeed, producing duplicate attendee rows for the same email (confidence 65, severity P2).

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler reads current attendees via `prisma.booking.findFirst(... include: { attendees: true })`, then computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering against that in-memory list, and finally inserts new attendees with `prisma.booking.update(... attendees: { createMany: { data: guestsFullDetails }})`. There is no transaction/locking shown and `createMany` is not using `skipDuplicates`, so concurrent `addGuests` calls can both pass the pre-check and then both attempt to insert the same (bookingId,email) pair(s). Whether this results in duplicate rows or a unique-constraint error depends on the DB schema (not shown in the diff), but the non-atomic check-then-insert race is clearly present in the diff and can cause incorrect behavior under concurrency.

The handler then performs `attendees.createMany` and triggers email sending over all attendees via `Promise.all`, so a single request can create/send an unbounded number of attendee records/emails, which is a verifiable resource-exhaustion/spam risk introduced by this change. adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, after loading the booking, the code proceeds to create attendee records (`prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`) and calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` without any guard on booking state (no check of a `status` field) or time (no check that `booking.endTime` is in the past). This means the new mutation can modify bookings regardless of whether they are cancelled/rejected/completed, which is a real behavioral defect if such states exist (the diff provides no counter-check elsewhere). The finding’s extra claim about `BookingListItem.tsx` rendering the action for past bookings is not directly verifiable from the shown diff, but the server-side missing validation is clearly present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:59 — Dialog uses onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog} directly with no reset handler, so closing via backdrop click/Escape (as opposed to the Cancel button) leaves isInvalidEmail=true and stale multiEmailValue in state; reopening the dialog immediately re-shows the "emails_must_be_unique_valid" error banner for a fresh attempt (confidence 70, severity P2).

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog, the Dialog is controlled via `open={isOpenDialog}` and `onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}` with no wrapper to reset local state on close.
